# @aihu/agent-acp

> DEPRECATED — use `@aihu/agent-a2a` instead. The BeeAI ACP protocol merged
> into the A2A protocol under the Linux Foundation in August 2025; there is no
> independent ACP spec left to conform to. This package is frozen at `0.1.x`
> (it still compiles and runs, but receives no further features). Mount
> `mountA2aAdapter` from `@aihu/agent-a2a` on the same `AgentService` to get
> the A2A v1.0.1 JSON-RPC binding with the same `resolveAuth` attribution.

`@aihu/agent-acp` is the deprecated ACP adapter for aihu. It bridges an `AgentService` (from `@aihu/agent-service`) to a pre-consolidation ACP-style message transport. New integrations should use `@aihu/agent-a2a`.

The package ships as ≤ 600 B gzipped (excluding `@aihu/agent-service`). Use it when your aihu app needs to participate in an ACP-based multi-agent system.

## Right idioms

### 1. Mount the ACP adapter on an existing `AgentService`

```ts
import { createAgentService } from '@aihu/agent-service'
import { mountAcpAdapter } from '@aihu/agent-acp'

const service = createAgentService({ manifest, invoke })
const adapter = mountAcpAdapter(service, {
  port: 3001,
  // optional: filter which actions are accessible via ACP
})
```

### 2. Use `AcpMessage` type for manual message construction in tests

```ts
import type { AcpMessage } from '@aihu/agent-acp'

const msg: AcpMessage = {
  type: 'tool_call',
  action: 'addTodo',
  params: { text: 'Write tests' },
  id: '123',
}
```

### 3. Dispose the adapter when the component disconnects

```ts
disconnectedCallback() {
  adapter.dispose()
  service.dispose?.()
  scope.dispose()
}
```

### 4. Set CORS and auth options in `AcpAdapterOptions` for production deployments

```ts
const adapter = mountAcpAdapter(service, {
  port: 3001,
  cors: { origin: 'https://my-orchestrator.example.com' },
  auth: (req) => req.headers.get('X-Api-Key') === process.env.API_KEY,
})
```

### 5. Keep the ACP adapter co-located with the component that owns the agent surface

Each ACP adapter instance corresponds to one component's agent surface. Do not share one adapter across multiple components with different manifests.

## Anti-patterns

### 1. Do not import ACP adapter in browser bundles — it is for Node/edge server environments

`@aihu/agent-acp` opens a network port or HTTP endpoint. It belongs in server-side entry points, not in client-side SFC bundles.

### 2. Do not skip authentication in production ACP endpoints

The adapter accepts incoming network connections. Without auth, any caller can invoke component actions.

### 3. Do not rely on ACP for in-page component communication — use signals directly

ACP is for cross-process or cross-network agent communication. For two components on the same page, use shared signals or `@aihu/context`.

### 4. Do not use `@aihu/agent-acp` without first registering the underlying component's agent metadata

The ACP adapter delegates to `AgentService`, which requires a valid `AgentManifest`. Missing manifest entries cause runtime errors on first tool call.

### 5. Do not manually parse `AcpMessage` payloads — let `mountAcpAdapter` handle deserialization

The adapter validates and routes messages. Duplicating this logic outside the adapter introduces drift between the schema and the handler.

## Canonical example files

- `packages/agent-acp/src/index.ts` — public API (mountAcpAdapter, types)
- `packages/agent-acp/src/acp-adapter.ts` — adapter implementation
- `packages/agent-acp/src/types.ts` — AcpAdapter, AcpAdapterOptions, AcpMessage
- `packages/agent-service/llms.txt` — AgentService setup (prerequisite)
